rationale:
Split into 3 children: one reuses a comparator-accepted DAG theorem with a byte-identical frozen type, and two are new.

(1) sq_sum = the accepted regcomp_covector_sq_sum_orthonormalBasis (node root.regular_components_are_minimizing-a1.imrep_mass_formula-a1.covector_sq_sum-a1, status accepted, candidate 16144a475b, isolated comparator passed). (2) pullback_le is new: dimred_mbl_dt_lp_cb_pullback_le, conjunct (L1), from steps 3–4.
(3) curry_le is new: dimred_mbl_dt_lp_cb_curryLeft_le, conjunct (L2), from step 5.

Why split:
- The selected theorem is exactly (L1) ∧ (L2), two independent bounds. Each is a reusable statement: the parent lipschitz_pushforward uses them separately, and byte-identical copies are requested in other branches (cmcdt_lp_covector_pullback_norm_le, dimred_mbl_pf_oc_covectorEuclideanNorm_comp_le, cmcdt_lp_covector_curryLeft_norm_le).
- Both bounds rest on (L0), which is already proved and accepted. Unsplit, this node has no dependencies and would have to re-prove (L0), about 130 Lean lines. Listing the accepted declaration as a child makes it a declared sibling dependency of both new children.
- The two new children are independent and can run in parallel.

Assembly by the supplied proof ("Steps 4 and 5 are the two conjuncts"): Submission.dimred_mbl_dt_lp_covector_bounds := ⟨Submission.dimred_mbl_dt_lp_cb_pullback_le, Submission.dimred_mbl_dt_lp_cb_curryLeft_le⟩. Steps 1–2 are sq_sum and step 3 is inside pullback_le.

- (L2): the count of tuples in which the index of f_1 occurs exactly once is written with position sums R_p, the swap symmetry R_p = R_0 and the multiplicity bound.

subproblems.title: Factorial Hilbert–Schmidt identity Σ_j α(f∘j)² = n!·|α|² in any orthonormal basis (parent (L0); reused accepted theorem)
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, let α be an n-covector on ℝ^P (α : Covector (Euclid P) n, a continuous alternating n-linear form on ℝ^P = Euclid P = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin P)), and let f = (f_0, …, f_{P−1}) be an orthonormal basis of ℝ^P indexed by Fin P (f : OrthonormalBasis (Fin P) ℝ (Euclid P)). Then Σ_{j : Fin n → Fin P} α(f_{j(0)}, …, f_{j(n−1)})² = n!·|α|², where the sum runs over all index tuples and |α| = covectorEuclideanNorm α = (Σ_{I : Fin n → Fin P strictly increasing} α(e_{I(0)}, …, e_{I(n−1)})²)^{1/2} with e = EuclideanSpace.basisFun (Fin P) ℝ the standard basis. This is identity (L0) of the parent proof, and it is exactly the comparator-accepted DAG theorem regcomp_covector_sq_sum_orthonormalBasis, reused with its identical frozen Lean type.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (α : Covector (Euclid P) n) (f : OrthonormalBasis (Fin P) ℝ (Euclid P)), ∑ j : Fin n → Fin P, (α (fun k => f (j k))) ^ 2 = (n.factorial : ℝ) * covectorEuclideanNorm α ^ 2
subproblems.natural_proof:
Reused accepted theorem. This child is identity (L0) of the selected parent proof (steps 1–2 there). Its frozen Lean type is byte-identical to the comparator-accepted DAG theorem regcomp_covector_sq_sum_orthonormalBasis (node root.regular_components_are_minimizing-a1.imrep_mass_formula-a1.covector_sq_sum-a1, status accepted, candidate 16144a475b272196ba8b2bd15f104028282dbcfc, isolated comparator passed), so that declaration is reused and not formalized again. The proof below is the parent's steps 1–2 with the details filled in. It is the argument formalized in the accepted candidate: Submission.regcomp_covector_sq_sum_basis_invariant carries out step 1 and Submission.regcomp_covector_sq_sum_basisFun carries out steps 2–6.

Notation. ℝ^P = Euclid P = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin P), and e_i := EuclideanSpace.basisFun (Fin P) ℝ i is the standard orthonormal basis. For a family b : Fin P → ℝ^P and j : Fin n → Fin P write b∘j := (b_{j(0)}, …, b_{j(n−1)}) (Lean: fun k => b (j k)). Put S_b(α) := Σ_{j : Fin n → Fin P} α(b∘j)², a sum over all index tuples. |α| := covectorEuclideanNorm α = √(Σ_{I : Fin n → Fin P} [I strictly increasing]·α(e∘I)²) (SimonGMT Chapter06/Mass.lean). We must show S_f(α) = n!·|α|².

1. (Basis independence, parent step 1.) Let b, b' be orthonormal bases of ℝ^P indexed by Fin P, and put c(i, s) := ⟨b'_s, b_i⟩. Then b_i = Σ_s c(i, s)·b'_s (OrthonormalBasis.sum_repr').
(a) Expansion. α is linear in each of its n slots. Expanding every slot (MultilinearMap.map_sum, then map_smul_univ) gives, for every j, α(b∘j) = Σ_{a : Fin n → Fin P} (Π_k c(j(k), a(k)))·α(b'∘a).
(b) Orthogonality. For s, t ∈ Fin P, Σ_i c(i, s)·c(i, t) = Σ_i ⟨b'_s, b_i⟩⟨b_i, b'_t⟩ = ⟨b'_s, b'_t⟩ = δ_{st}. This is Parseval for b (OrthonormalBasis.sum_inner_mul_inner) followed by orthonormality of b' (orthonormal_iff_ite). Here O_{si} = c(i, s) is the parent's orthogonal matrix.
(c) Slot sums. For a, a' : Fin n → Fin P, the sum over j factors over the slots (Fintype.prod_sum): Σ_{j : Fin n → Fin P} Π_k c(j(k), a(k))·c(j(k), a'(k)) = Π_k Σ_i c(i, a(k))·c(i, a'(k)) = Π_k δ_{a(k) a'(k)}. This equals 1 if a = a' and 0 otherwise.
(d) Squaring (a) and summing over j: S_b(α) = Σ_j Σ_a Σ_{a'} α(b'∘a)·α(b'∘a')·Π_k c(j(k), a(k))·c(j(k), a'(k)). Exchanging the finite sums and using (c), this is Σ_a Σ_{a'} α(b'∘a)·α(b'∘a')·[a = a'] = Σ_a α(b'∘a)² = S_{b'}(α).

2. (Square of the norm.) The radicand of |α| is a finite sum of nonnegative terms. Hence |α|² = Σ_{I strictly increasing} α(e∘I)² (Real.sq_sqrt).

3. (Non-injective tuples vanish.) If j is not injective, say j(p) = j(q) with p ≠ q, then the tuple e∘j has the equal entries e_{j(p)} = e_{j(q)} in the distinct slots p and q, so e∘j is not injective (Function.Injective.of_comp). Since α is alternating, α(e∘j) = 0 (ContinuousAlternatingMap.map_eq_zero_of_not_injective). Hence S_e(α) = Σ_{j injective} α(e∘j)².

4. (Injective tuples = increasing tuples × permutations.) The map (I, π) ↦ I∘π is a bijection from {I : Fin n → Fin P strictly increasing} × Perm(Fin n) onto {j : Fin n → Fin P injective}.
- It lands in the injective tuples, since I and π are injective.
- It is injective. If I∘π = I'∘π', then range I = range I'. A strictly increasing map out of Fin n is determined by its range (StrictMono.range_inj_of_wellFoundedLT), so I = I'. Then π = π' because I is injective.
- It is surjective. Let j be injective and σ := Tuple.sort j. Then j∘σ is monotone (Tuple.monotone_sort) and injective, hence strictly increasing, and j = (j∘σ)∘σ⁻¹.

5. (Signs.) For π ∈ Perm(Fin n), α(e∘(I∘π)) = sign(π)·α(e∘I) (AlternatingMap.map_perm applied to α.toAlternatingMap). Since sign(π) = ±1, α(e∘(I∘π))² = α(e∘I)².

6. (Count.) Reindex the sum of step 3 by the bijection of step 4 (Finset.sum_bij) and use step 5: S_e(α) = Σ_{I strictly increasing} Σ_{π ∈ Perm(Fin n)} α(e∘I)². Since |Perm(Fin n)| = n! (Fintype.card_perm, Fintype.card_fin), this is n!·Σ_{I strictly increasing} α(e∘I)² = n!·|α|² by step 2.

7. (Conclusion.) Step 1 with (b, b') := (f, e), then step 6: Σ_{j : Fin n → Fin P} α(f∘j)² = S_f(α) = S_e(α) = n!·|α|². That is, ∑ j : Fin n → Fin P, (α (fun k => f (j k))) ^ 2 = (n.factorial : ℝ) * covectorEuclideanNorm α ^ 2. The argument is uniform in n and P. For n = 0 there is one empty tuple, it is strictly increasing, and 0! = 1. For n > P there are no injective and no strictly increasing tuples, so both sides are 0. ∎
proof_key_steps: Basis independence (parent step 1): expand every slot in the second basis by multilinearity; Σ_i c(i,s)c(i,t) = δ_st kills all cross terms, so S_b(α) = S_{b'}(α).
|α|² equals the sum of α(e∘I)² over strictly increasing I; non-injective tuples contribute 0 since α is alternating.
(I, π) ↦ I∘π is a bijection from increasing tuples × permutations onto injective tuples, and α(e∘(I∘π))² = α(e∘I)².
Counting n! permutations gives S_e(α) = n!·|α|², hence S_f(α) = n!·|α|² for every orthonormal basis f.

subproblems.title: Pull-back bound |A^#β| ≤ ‖A‖^k·|β| for the Euclidean coefficient norm of covectors (parent (L1))
subproblems.statement: Let N, N', k ∈ ℕ, let A : ℝ^N → ℝ^{N'} be a continuous linear map (A : Euclid N →L[ℝ] Euclid N') with operator norm ‖A‖ (for the Euclidean norms), and let β be a k-covector on ℝ^{N'} (β : Covector (Euclid N') k). Let A^#β := β.compContinuousLinearMap A be its pull-back, (A^#β)(w_1, …, w_k) = β(Aw_1, …, Aw_k). Then |A^#β| ≤ ‖A‖^k·|β|, where for a covector α on ℝ^M, |α| = covectorEuclideanNorm α is the Euclidean norm of the values of α on the strictly increasing tuples of standard basis vectors of ℝ^M.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (N N' k : ℕ) (A : Euclid N →L[ℝ] Euclid N') (β : Covector (Euclid N') k), covectorEuclideanNorm (β.compContinuousLinearMap A) ≤ ‖A‖ ^ k * covectorEuclideanNorm β
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: steps 3–4 of the selected parent proof, specialized and completed. Those steps are the one-slot estimate T_j ≤ ‖A‖²·T_{j−1}, iterated over the k slots, followed by (L0) from step 2. Here the telescoping chain T_k ≤ ‖A‖²·T_{k−1} ≤ … ≤ ‖A‖^{2k}·T_0 is organized as an induction on the degree that peels off the first slot with curryLeft. Each induction step is one application of the parent's one-slot estimate. Uses the sibling sq_sum (Submission.regcomp_covector_sq_sum_orthonormalBasis), which is identity (L0).

Notation. ℝ^M = Euclid M = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin M). Slots of an m-covector are indexed by Fin m = {0, …, m−1}, so the statement's (w_1, …, w_k) is written (w_0, …, w_{k−1}) below. e = (e_a)_{a ∈ Fin N} := EuclideanSpace.basisFun (Fin N) ℝ is the standard orthonormal basis of ℝ^N, and e' = (e'_b)_{b ∈ Fin N'} := EuclideanSpace.basisFun (Fin N') ℝ is that of ℝ^{N'}.
- For an m-covector γ on ℝ^M, a family b : Fin M → ℝ^M and j : Fin m → Fin M, write b∘j := (b_{j(0)}, …, b_{j(m−1)}) (Lean: fun i => b (j i)) and S_b(γ) := Σ_{j : Fin m → Fin M} γ(b∘j)².
- |α| := covectorEuclideanNorm α.
- For x ∈ ℝ^M and an (m+1)-covector γ on ℝ^M, ι_xγ := γ.curryLeft x is the m-covector w ↦ γ(x, w_0, …, w_{m−1}) (ContinuousAlternatingMap.curryLeft_apply_apply: γ.curryLeft x w = γ (Matrix.vecCons x w)). The map γ.curryLeft : ℝ^M →L[ℝ] Covector (ℝ^M) m is continuous linear in x.
- For an m-covector γ on ℝ^{N'}, A^#γ := γ.compContinuousLinearMap A, so (A^#γ)(w) = γ(A∘w) = γ(Aw_0, …, Aw_{m−1}) (ContinuousAlternatingMap.compContinuousLinearMap_apply).

1. (Parseval for functionals.) Let M ∈ ℕ, let e^{(M)}_a := EuclideanSpace.basisFun (Fin M) ℝ a, and let μ : ℝ^M →L[ℝ] ℝ be continuous linear. Then Σ_{a ∈ Fin M} μ(e^{(M)}_a)² = ‖μ‖².
Proof. Let g := (InnerProductSpace.toDual ℝ ℝ^M).symm μ be the Riesz vector of μ. Then ⟨g, x⟩ = μ(x) for all x (InnerProductSpace.toDual_symm_apply). Also ‖g‖ = ‖μ‖, because toDual is a linear isometric equivalence (LinearIsometryEquiv.norm_map). Parseval for the orthonormal basis e^{(M)} (OrthonormalBasis.sum_inner_mul_inner g g) gives Σ_a ⟨g, e^{(M)}_a⟩·⟨e^{(M)}_a, g⟩ = ⟨g, g⟩ = ‖g‖² (real_inner_self_eq_norm_sq). Each factor equals μ(e^{(M)}_a) by real_inner_comm, so Σ_a μ(e^{(M)}_a)² = ‖g‖² = ‖μ‖². For M = N the basis e^{(N)} is e; for M = N' it is e'.

2. (One-slot estimate, parent step 3.) For every continuous linear functional μ : ℝ^{N'} →L[ℝ] ℝ,
Σ_{a ∈ Fin N} μ(Ae_a)² ≤ ‖A‖²·Σ_{b ∈ Fin N'} μ(e'_b)².
Proof. μ∘A := μ.comp A is a continuous linear functional on ℝ^N with (μ∘A)(e_a) = μ(Ae_a). By step 1 with M = N, the left side equals ‖μ∘A‖². By step 1 with M = N', the right side equals ‖A‖²·‖μ‖². Since 0 ≤ ‖μ∘A‖ ≤ ‖μ‖·‖A‖ (ContinuousLinearMap.opNorm_comp_le), squaring (pow_le_pow_left₀) gives ‖μ∘A‖² ≤ (‖μ‖·‖A‖)² = ‖A‖²·‖μ‖². This is the parent's computation: if μ = ⟨g, ·⟩, then μ∘A = ⟨A*g, ·⟩ and Σ_i ⟨g, Ae_i⟩² = |A*g|² ≤ ‖A‖²·|g|².

3. (First-slot reindexing.) For M, m ∈ ℕ and every F : (Fin (m+1) → Fin M) → ℝ,
Σ_{J : Fin (m+1) → Fin M} F(J) = Σ_{a ∈ Fin M} Σ_{j : Fin m → Fin M} F(Fin.cons a j).
This holds because (a, j) ↦ Fin.cons a j is a bijection Fin M × (Fin m → Fin M) ≃ (Fin (m+1) → Fin M) (Fin.consEquiv; Fintype.sum_equiv and Fintype.sum_prod_type). Moreover, for every (m+1)-covector γ on ℝ^M and every family b : Fin M → ℝ^M, γ(b∘Fin.cons a j) = (ι_{b_a}γ)(b∘j). Indeed b∘Fin.cons a j = Matrix.vecCons b_a (b∘j): both agree on slot 0 and on every slot i.succ (Fin.cases). Then apply curryLeft_apply_apply.

4. (Hilbert–Schmidt inequality, the parent's chain of one-slot estimates.) Claim H(m), for every m ∈ ℕ: every m-covector γ on ℝ^{N'} satisfies S_e(A^#γ) ≤ (‖A‖²)^m·S_{e'}(γ), that is,
Σ_{j : Fin m → Fin N} (A^#γ)(e∘j)² ≤ (‖A‖²)^m·Σ_{j : Fin m → Fin N'} γ(e'∘j)².
The proof is by induction on m, for all γ simultaneously.
(a) m = 0. Each of Fin 0 → Fin N and Fin 0 → Fin N' has exactly one element (Fintype.sum_unique). The two argument tuples A∘(e∘j) and e'∘j' are maps out of Fin 0, hence equal (Subsingleton.elim). So both sums consist of the same single term γ(∅)², and (‖A‖²)^0 = 1.
(b) Step m → m+1. Let γ be an (m+1)-covector on ℝ^{N'}.
- By step 3 with M = N and b = e, S_e(A^#γ) = Σ_{a ∈ Fin N} Σ_{j : Fin m → Fin N} (ι_{e_a}(A^#γ))(e∘j)².
- For every x ∈ ℝ^N, ι_x(A^#γ) = A^#(ι_{Ax}γ), since both send w to γ(Ax, Aw_0, …, Aw_{m−1}) (Mathlib ContinuousAlternatingMap.curryLeft_compContinuousLinearMap). Hence S_e(A^#γ) = Σ_a S_e(A^#(ι_{Ae_a}γ)).
- Apply H(m) to the m-covector ι_{Ae_a}γ for each a, then exchange the finite sums (Finset.mul_sum, Finset.sum_comm):
S_e(A^#γ) ≤ Σ_a (‖A‖²)^m·Σ_{j : Fin m → Fin N'} (ι_{Ae_a}γ)(e'∘j)² = (‖A‖²)^m·Σ_{j : Fin m → Fin N'} Σ_{a ∈ Fin N} μ_j(Ae_a)².
Here, for fixed j, μ_j := (ContinuousAlternatingMap.apply ℝ (Euclid N') ℝ (e'∘j)).comp γ.curryLeft : ℝ^{N'} →L[ℝ] ℝ is the continuous linear functional μ_j(u) = (ι_uγ)(e'∘j) = γ(u, e'_{j(0)}, …, e'_{j(m−1)}).
- By step 2, Σ_a μ_j(Ae_a)² ≤ ‖A‖²·Σ_{b ∈ Fin N'} μ_j(e'_b)² for every j. Multiply by (‖A‖²)^m ≥ 0 and sum over j (monotonicity of finite sums; gcongr).
- Exchange the sums again and use (‖A‖²)^m·‖A‖² = (‖A‖²)^{m+1} (pow_succ):
S_e(A^#γ) ≤ (‖A‖²)^{m+1}·Σ_{b ∈ Fin N'} Σ_{j : Fin m → Fin N'} (ι_{e'_b}γ)(e'∘j)².
- By step 3 with M = N' and b = e', the double sum equals Σ_b Σ_j γ(e'∘Fin.cons b j)² = S_{e'}(γ). This proves H(m+1).

5. (Factorial identity (L0).) Apply the sibling sq_sum (Submission.regcomp_covector_sq_sum_orthonormalBasis) twice:
- with (P, n, α, f) := (N, k, A^#β, EuclideanSpace.basisFun (Fin N) ℝ), giving S_e(A^#β) = k!·|A^#β|²;
- with (P, n, α, f) := (N', k, β, EuclideanSpace.basisFun (Fin N') ℝ), giving S_{e'}(β) = k!·|β|².

6. (Conclusion.) H(k) for γ := β and step 5 give k!·|A^#β|² ≤ (‖A‖²)^k·k!·|β|². Since k! > 0 (Nat.factorial_pos), |A^#β|² ≤ (‖A‖²)^k·|β|² = (‖A‖^k·|β|)² (pow_mul, mul_pow). Both |A^#β| and ‖A‖^k·|β| are ≥ 0 (covectorEuclideanNorm_nonneg, norm_nonneg). Therefore |A^#β| ≤ ‖A‖^k·|β| (pow_le_pow_iff_left₀ with exponent 2). That is, covectorEuclideanNorm (β.compContinuousLinearMap A) ≤ ‖A‖ ^ k * covectorEuclideanNorm β. The argument is uniform. For k = 0, H(0) is an equality and the conclusion reads |A^#β| ≤ 1·|β|. For N = 0 or N' = 0 all sums are finite and the same steps apply. ∎
proof_key_steps: Parseval for functionals Σ_a μ(e_a)² = ‖μ‖² (Riesz vector, OrthonormalBasis.sum_inner_mul_inner); hence the one-slot estimate Σ_a μ(Ae_a)² ≤ ‖A‖²·Σ_b μ(e'_b)² from ‖μ∘A‖ ≤ ‖μ‖·‖A‖.
First-slot reindexing J = Fin.cons a j (Fin.consEquiv) with γ(b∘Fin.cons a j) = (ι_{b_a}γ)(b∘j), and ι_x(A^#γ) = A^#(ι_{Ax}γ) (curryLeft_compContinuousLinearMap).
Hilbert–Schmidt inequality S_e(A^#γ) ≤ (‖A‖²)^m·S_{e'}(γ) by induction on m: induction hypothesis for ι_{Ae_a}γ, then the one-slot estimate for μ_j(u) = (ι_uγ)(e'∘j).
sq_sum turns S_e(A^#β) and S_{e'}(β) into k!·|A^#β|² and k!·|β|²; cancel k! and take square roots of nonnegative numbers.

subproblems.title: Interior-product bound |ι_vβ| ≤ ‖v‖·|β| for the Euclidean coefficient norm of covectors (parent (L2))
subproblems.statement: Let N, k ∈ ℕ, let v ∈ ℝ^N (v : Euclid N) and let β be a (k+1)-covector on ℝ^N (β : Covector (Euclid N) (k + 1)). Let ι_vβ := β.curryLeft v be the interior product, the k-covector (ι_vβ)(w_1, …, w_k) = β(v, w_1, …, w_k). Then |ι_vβ| ≤ ‖v‖·|β|, where ‖v‖ is the Euclidean norm of v and, for a covector α on ℝ^N, |α| = covectorEuclideanNorm α is the Euclidean norm of the values of α on the strictly increasing tuples of standard basis vectors.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (N k : ℕ) (v : Euclid N) (β : Covector (Euclid N) (k + 1)), covectorEuclideanNorm (β.curryLeft v) ≤ ‖v‖ * covectorEuclideanNorm β
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: step 5 of the selected parent proof, specialized and completed. That step normalizes v, extends v/|v| to an orthonormal basis f, and compares the Hilbert–Schmidt sums of ι_{f_1}β and β by keeping only the tuples in which the index of f_1 occurs exactly once. Here the bookkeeping "position p at which that index occurs" is written with the position sums R_p below. Uses the sibling sq_sum (Submission.regcomp_covector_sq_sum_orthonormalBasis), which is identity (L0).

Notation. ℝ^N = Euclid N with standard orthonormal basis e = EuclideanSpace.basisFun (Fin N) ℝ. Slots of an m-covector are indexed by Fin m = {0, …, m−1}, so the statement's (w_1, …, w_k) is written (w_0, …, w_{k−1}) below.
- For a family b : Fin N → ℝ^N (such as e or an orthonormal basis f of ℝ^N indexed by Fin N) and J : Fin m → Fin N, b∘J := (b_{J(0)}, …, b_{J(m−1)}) (Lean: fun i => b (J i)).
- For an m-covector α on ℝ^N, |α| := covectorEuclideanNorm α = √(Σ_{I : Fin m → Fin N} [I strictly increasing]·α(e∘I)²).
- For x ∈ ℝ^N, ι_xβ := β.curryLeft x is the k-covector w ↦ β(x, w_0, …, w_{k−1}) (ContinuousAlternatingMap.curryLeft_apply_apply: β.curryLeft x w = β (Matrix.vecCons x w)). The map β.curryLeft : ℝ^N →L[ℝ] Covector (ℝ^N) k is linear in x.

1. (Homogeneity of the coefficient norm.) For c ∈ ℝ and a k-covector γ on ℝ^N, |c•γ| = |c|·|γ|.
Each coefficient satisfies (c•γ)(e∘I) = c·γ(e∘I), so (c•γ)(e∘I)² = c²·γ(e∘I)². Hence the radicand of |c•γ| equals c²·X, where X ≥ 0 is the radicand of |γ| (Finset.mul_sum, termwise on both branches of `if StrictMono I`). Therefore |c•γ| = √(c²·X) = √(c²)·√X = |c|·|γ| (Real.sqrt_mul with c² ≥ 0, Real.sqrt_sq_eq_abs).

2. (Case v = 0.) β.curryLeft 0 = 0 (map_zero), so |ι_0β| = 0 (covectorEuclideanNorm_zero) and ‖0‖·|β| = 0. From now on assume v ≠ 0. Then N ≥ 1: for N = 0, ℝ^0 is a subsingleton and v would be 0. Put i₀ := ⟨0, _⟩ ∈ Fin N.

3. (Rotating v to a basis vector.) ‖v‖ > 0. Put u := ‖v‖⁻¹•v. Then ‖u‖ = ‖v‖⁻¹·‖v‖ = 1 (norm_smul, norm_inv, norm_norm) and v = ‖v‖•u (smul_smul, mul_inv_cancel₀).
- Let s := {i₀} ⊆ Fin N. The family indexed by s with constant value u is orthonormal: its only member has norm 1, and s contains no two distinct indices.
- finrank ℝ ℝ^N = N = card(Fin N). So Orthonormal.exists_orthonormalBasis_extension_of_card_eq (with v := fun _ => u and s := {i₀}) gives an orthonormal basis f : OrthonormalBasis (Fin N) ℝ (Euclid N) with f(i₀) = u.
- β.curryLeft is linear, so ι_vβ = ι_{‖v‖•u}β = ‖v‖•ι_uβ (map_smul). By step 1 and ‖v‖ ≥ 0, |ι_vβ| = ‖v‖·|ι_uβ|.
Hence it suffices to prove |ι_uβ| ≤ |β|. Then |ι_vβ| = ‖v‖·|ι_uβ| ≤ ‖v‖·|β| (mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left).

4. (Position sums.) For J : Fin (k+1) → Fin N put g(J) := β(f∘J)² ≥ 0. For p ∈ Fin (k+1) put R_p := Σ_{J : Fin (k+1) → Fin N} [J(p) = i₀]·g(J) (Lean: ∑ J, if J p = i₀ then g J else 0).

5. (R_0 = k!·|ι_uβ|².) The map (a, j) ↦ Fin.cons a j is a bijection Fin N × (Fin k → Fin N) → (Fin (k+1) → Fin N) (Fin.consEquiv). Under it J(0) = a (Fin.cons_zero), so
R_0 = Σ_{a ∈ Fin N} Σ_{j : Fin k → Fin N} [a = i₀]·g(Fin.cons a j) = Σ_{j : Fin k → Fin N} g(Fin.cons i₀ j) (Fintype.sum_eq_single i₀).
Now f∘Fin.cons i₀ j = Matrix.vecCons (f i₀) (f∘j) = Matrix.vecCons u (f∘j): check slot 0 and every slot i.succ (Fin.cases). So g(Fin.cons i₀ j) = β(Matrix.vecCons u (f∘j))² = (ι_uβ)(f∘j)² (curryLeft_apply_apply). Hence R_0 = Σ_{j : Fin k → Fin N} (ι_uβ)(f∘j)², and this equals k!·|ι_uβ|² by sq_sum applied to (P, n, α, f) := (N, k, ι_uβ, f).

6. (R_p = R_0 for every p ∈ Fin (k+1).) Let σ := Equiv.swap 0 p ∈ Perm(Fin (k+1)); it is the identity if p = 0. Then σ⁻¹ = σ (Equiv.symm_swap) and σ(p) = 0 (Equiv.swap_apply_right).
- J ↦ J∘σ is a bijection of Fin (k+1) → Fin N: it is σ.arrowCongr (Equiv.refl (Fin N)), whose value at J is J∘σ⁻¹ = J∘σ. Substituting (Equiv.sum_comp), R_p = Σ_J [(J∘σ)(p) = i₀]·g(J∘σ).
- (J∘σ)(p) = J(σ p) = J(0).
- f∘(J∘σ) = (f∘J)∘σ, so β(f∘(J∘σ)) = sign(σ)·β(f∘J) (AlternatingMap.map_perm on β.toAlternatingMap). Since sign(σ) = ±1 (Int.units_eq_one_or), g(J∘σ) = g(J).
Therefore R_p = Σ_J [J(0) = i₀]·g(J) = R_0. This is the parent's remark that moving f_{i₀} to the front only permutes the arguments, so β(f_{I'}) = ±β(f_{i₀}, f_I).

7. (Σ_p R_p ≤ Σ_J g(J).) Exchanging the finite sums (Finset.sum_comm), Σ_p R_p = Σ_J Σ_p [J(p) = i₀]·g(J). It suffices to show Σ_p [J(p) = i₀]·g(J) ≤ g(J) for every J.
- Case 1: there are positions p ≠ q with J(p) = J(q) = i₀. Then the tuple f∘J has the equal entries f_{i₀} in the distinct slots p and q. Since β is alternating, β(f∘J) = 0 (ContinuousAlternatingMap.map_eq_zero_of_eq). So g(J) = 0 and both sides are 0.
- Case 2: otherwise. The set {p : J(p) = i₀} has at most one element (Finset.card_le_one). So Σ_p [J(p) = i₀]·g(J) = #{p : J(p) = i₀}·g(J) ≤ 1·g(J) = g(J) (Finset.sum_ite, Finset.sum_const, g(J) ≥ 0).
This is the parent's restriction to the tuples in which i₀ occurs exactly once: tuples containing i₀ at least twice contribute 0, and the dropped terms are ≥ 0.

8. (Total sum.) Σ_{J : Fin (k+1) → Fin N} g(J) = (k+1)!·|β|², by sq_sum applied to (P, n, α, f) := (N, k+1, β, f).

9. (Conclusion.) By step 6, Σ_p R_p = (k+1)·R_0. Combine this with steps 5, 7 and 8 and with (k+1)! = (k+1)·k! (Nat.factorial_succ): (k+1)·k!·|ι_uβ|² ≤ (k+1)·k!·|β|². Since (k+1)·k! > 0, |ι_uβ|² ≤ |β|². Both norms are ≥ 0 (covectorEuclideanNorm_nonneg), so |ι_uβ| ≤ |β| (pow_le_pow_iff_left₀ with exponent 2). By step 3, |ι_vβ| = ‖v‖·|ι_uβ| ≤ ‖v‖·|β|, that is, covectorEuclideanNorm (β.curryLeft v) ≤ ‖v‖ * covectorEuclideanNorm β. The argument is uniform. k = 0 needs no separate case: Fin 0 → Fin N has one element and 0! = 1. Nor does k+1 > N: every J then repeats an index, so all g(J) and R_p vanish. ∎
proof_key_steps: Homogeneity |c•γ| = |c|·|γ| and the case v = 0; otherwise reduce to u = v/‖v‖ = f(i₀) for an orthonormal basis f (Orthonormal.exists_orthonormalBasis_extension_of_card_eq).
Position sums R_p := Σ_J [J(p) = i₀]·β(f∘J)²; R_0 = k!·|ι_uβ|² by Fin.cons reindexing and sq_sum.
R_p = R_0 for every p via the transposition swap 0 p (sign² = 1).
Σ_p R_p ≤ Σ_J β(f∘J)² = (k+1)!·|β|², because tuples containing i₀ twice vanish; hence |ι_uβ| ≤ |β| and |ι_vβ| ≤ ‖v‖·|β|.
